From: Lisa Hammond <procurement@cloudwave.com>

Subject: CloudWave reseller addendum - pass-through items (redlines attached)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the draft MSA + order form. Attached is CloudWave's redline (CloudWave_Reseller_Addendum_v2.pdf) — the procurement team flagged a few pass-through items that need clarification before we can move this to our legal queue: 

1) Marketplace fees: our standard marketplace model requires that platform/marketplace fees be presented as a pass-through line item on invoices to end customers. Your draft appears to roll those into a single line. Can you confirm whether Redwood can present a discrete marketplace fee on invoices or if Redwood expects the reseller to handle the pass-through?

2) Tax & surcharge treatment: if VAT/sales tax is applicable, CloudWave requires that taxes be shown separately and that resellers cannot re-characterize tax as a markup. We redlined a carve-out that prohibits surcharging taxes; please advise if Redwood needs an exception for specific reseller scenarios.

3) Audit & evidence: we need to understand the audit mechanics. The redline currently allows CloudWave or its auditors to request invoice-level evidence and, if needed, a site visit clause. Please confirm: a) frequency (we prefer annual), b) scope limitations, and c) any existing customer-facing templates you can share to speed this up.

4) Invoice waterfall / allocation: CloudWave wants the order form to specify the invoice waterfall for fee allocation (platform -> marketplace -> reseller) and an agreed reconciliation cadence. The current order form draft does not show an allocation waterfall.

Would you be able to respond with suggested language on these four points by EOD Friday? If helpful, I'm available for a 30-minute call Monday morning.

Best,
Lisa Hammond
Sr. Procurement Manager
CloudWave Marketplace

Jordan / team / Lisa — thanks for the heads-up. I reviewed CloudWave's redlines and drafted narrower language to balance CloudWave's verification needs with Redwood's operational constraints. High-level points below plus proposed text (inserted into the attached RI-OrderForm-Draft):

1) Marketplace fee presentation
- Positioning: Redwood can render a discrete "Marketplace fee" line on invoices produced by Redwood's platform. However, where a reseller controls invoicing to end customers (self-billed), Redwood requires the reseller to display the marketplace fee as a separate line item or provide structured metadata in the invoice feed.
- Proposed language: "Marketplace Fee: Redwood or its authorized reseller shall itemize Marketplace Fees as a discrete line on customer invoices or include Marketplace Fee metadata in any self-billed invoice feed to CloudWave."

2) Taxes & surcharges
- We can't accept a broad ban on surcharges tied to bona fide taxes. Compromise: prohibit labeling taxes as a markup, but allow a limited reseller surcharge where local law permits an administrative fee; reseller must provide monthly supporting documentation.
- Proposed language: "Taxes shall be shown separately from any reseller administrative fees. Resellers may apply administrative surcharges only to the extent permitted by applicable law and must provide supporting documentation on a monthly basis."

3) Audit & evidence
- Frequency & scope: limit to no more than one full audit per 12-month period, with targeted, documented requests permitted more frequently if material discrepancies are identified (materiality threshold: 2% of annualized fees).
- Remote-first approach: CloudWave may request an "evidence bundle" (invoices, metadata, payment receipts) within 30 days. On-site audits require 60 days' notice and are subject to reasonable scope limits and NDA.
- Proposed language: "CloudWave may request documentation to verify Marketplace Fee allocation no more than once per 12-month period. Parties agree that an evidence bundle sufficient to substantiate invoices is the primary mechanism; on-site audits require 60 days' notice, are limited to a 12-month lookback and are subject to a mutually agreed scope and confidentiality agreement."

4) Invoice waterfall & reconciliation cadence
- Suggested default waterfall: Platform Fee -> Marketplace Fee -> Reseller Fee -> Taxes.
- Reconciliation cadence: offer monthly reconciliations by default, with an option for quarterly reconciliations for resellers with < $50k/month in marketplace transactions.
- Proposed language: "Invoices will reflect the following waterfall: Platform Fee; Marketplace Fee; Reseller Fee; Taxes. Parties may elect quarterly reconciliations where monthly reconciliation would impose undue operational burden as measured by transaction volume."

Attachments: I added tracked changes to RI-OrderForm-Draft-20270623.docx and included an updated flowchart-invoice-waterfall.png.

If CloudWave accepts the evidence-bundle-first approach and agrees to the audit frequency cap, I think we can finalize these sections without additional escalation.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Jordan / Kimberly / Lisa — thanks for the clear proposal. Tango is generally comfortable with the narrower language Kimberly suggested, with two minor exceptions: 

1) Reconciliation cadence: Tango requests quarterly reconciliations (instead of monthly) for marketplace customers under $100k ARR to reduce monthly ops load. They are happy to provide a monthly "summary file" (aggregated stats) if CloudWave requires more visibility.

2) Audit evidence: Tango prefers a pre-agreed sample set of invoices (three months spread across a 12-month window) in lieu of a full evidence bundle for the first audit; Tango will provide the sample invoices plus metadata and vendor receipts. If the sample shows material variance (>2%) CloudWave can then request a full evidence bundle.
